boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public-facing destinations on campus-adjacent Gainesville corridors, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Alachua County Library District Headquarters
cards.subtitle: East University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the headquarters branch at 401 E. University Ave. when your route runs east from campus toward downtown and you need a public-library stop.
cards.short_summary: A named public-library destination on East University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alachua County Library District identifies its Headquarters at 401 E. University Avenue in Gainesville.
cards.source_title: Alachua County Library District Long Range Plan
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current branch page for service and building hours.

cards.title: Matheson History Museum
cards.subtitle: East University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 513 E. University Ave. for exhibits focused on Gainesville, Alachua County, and Florida history; confirm reopening information before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A downtown history museum with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is located at 513 East University Avenue, presents local-history exhibitions, and lists free admission.
cards.access_notes: The museum’s visit page lists Wednesday–Saturday hours and notices temporary closures; check it before visiting.

cards.title: Bo Diddley Plaza
cards.subtitle: East University Avenue and Southeast First Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the covered-stage plaza as a downtown waypoint; the city documents it as a venue for concerts, festivals, gatherings, and picnic time.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown plaza built around a covered stage.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Gainesville describes Bo Diddley Plaza at Southeast First Street and East University Avenue as a venue for concerts, festivals, and gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Programming varies; consult the City of Gainesville events calendar for scheduled activities.

cards.title: Hippodrome State Theatre
cards.subtitle: Southeast Second Place corridor, beside Southwest First Avenue
cards.notes: Check the Hippodrome’s current ticket calendar when passing the downtown pedestrian-corridor area; its mainstage is at 25 SE 2nd Place.
cards.short_summary: A downtown theatre destination with scheduled ticketed performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hippodrome identifies its legal address as 25 SE 2nd Place, Gainesville, and its ticketing page lists mainstage performances there.
cards.source_title: The Hippodrome State Theatre: Planned Giving
cards.access_notes: Performance access and ticket availability vary by production; consult the theatre’s current schedule.

cards.title: Cade Museum for Creativity & Invention
cards.subtitle: South Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Head south on Main Street to the Cade at 811 S. Main St.; use its current visit page to choose an open day and obtain admission tickets.
cards.short_summary: A creativity-and-invention museum on South Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cade Museum lists its address as 811 South Main Street, Gainesville, and directs visitors to get tickets.
cards.source_title: Cade Museum for Creativity & Invention: Sitemap
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Thursday–Sunday opening, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; verify ticketing and any changes before arrival.

cards.title: Depot Park
cards.subtitle: Southeast Fourth Street corridor
cards.notes: Make Depot Park a destination along the southeast downtown route for its main pond and park setting; plan to leave before the city’s posted nightly closing time.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown park along the Southeast Fourth Street route.
cards.evidence_claim: A City of Gainesville communication states that Depot Park closes to the public each night at 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville Commissioner Mail Archive: Depot Park closing information
cards.access_notes: The City states the park closes nightly at 11 p.m.; do not remain after closing.

cards.title: Cotton Club Museum & Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Southeast Seventh Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit 837 SE 7th Ave. for exhibitions and programming centered on African-derived cultures, Gainesville history, and the African American music legacy.
cards.short_summary: A cultural institution in east downtown Gainesville.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cotton Club Museum & Cultural Center lists its location at 837 SE 7th Avenue and its mission includes preserving and sharing African American history and culture.
cards.source_title: Cotton Club Museum & Cultural Center: About Us
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Wednesday, Thursday, and Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; check its site for event-specific access.

cards.entity_name: A. Quinn Jones Museum & Cultural Center
cards.title: A. Quinn Jones Museum & Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Northwest Seventh Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Follow Northwest Seventh Avenue to the former Jones family home for its permanent Prof Jones exhibit, neighborhood history, oral histories, and rotating displays.
cards.short_summary: A city museum documenting educator A. Quinn Jones and local history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the museum at 1013 NW Seventh Avenue occupies the former Jones family home and presents exhibits and oral histories about Gainesville’s African American experience.
cards.source_title: City of Gainesville: A. Quinn Jones Museum & Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: The City lists Tuesday–Friday hours of 1–5 p.m., plus access by appointment and during special events.

cards.entity_name: The Historic Thomas Center Museum and Art Galleries
cards.title: The Historic Thomas Center Museum and Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: Northeast Sixth Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk Northeast Sixth Avenue to 302 NE Sixth Ave. to see the historic center, its art-gallery spaces, restored rooms, and gardens.
cards.short_summary: A city cultural center with galleries, historic spaces, and gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies the Historic Thomas Center at 302 NE Sixth Avenue and describes it as a cultural events center with contemporary art exhibitions and historical exhibits.
cards.access_notes: Check the City’s Thomas Center page for gallery and event access before visiting.

cards.title: Rosa B. Williams Center
cards.subtitle: Northwest First Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Rosa B. Williams Center at 524 NW First St. as a stop for participatory arts programming, including dance, music, gallery, and community art activities.
cards.short_summary: A named participatory-arts center near the Fifth Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the Rosa B. Williams Center at 524 NW First Street as a participatory arts space with gallery and dance facilities.
cards.access_notes: Classes and events vary; consult the City’s venue and events listings for current opportunities.
